newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Lonsum sees 1997 net at 101 bln rph.
newsitem.headline: Lonsum sees 1997 net at 101 bln rph.

text.p: Indonesian plantation firm PT PP London Sumatra Indonesia (Lonsum) said on Thursday it expected to post a net profit of 101 billion rupiah in 1997 against an expected 73 billion rupiah in 1996.
"Next year we expect to achieve (a net profit of) 101 billion rupiah. This year we expect 73 billion rupiah," senior Lonsum official Agnes Safford told Reuters.
She said Lonsum was confident of achieving the target following higher-than-expected profits in the first nine months of this year.
London Sumatra announced on Wednesday that it posted a net profit of 54.45 billion rupiah in the first nine months of 1996 against 42.65 billion rupiah in the same period last year.
Safford said prices of both palm oil and rubber were likely to be firm and the forecast looked easily achievable.
Lonsum posted crude palm oil (CPO) sales of 68,427 tonnes, with an average export selling price of $583 per tonne as of September 30 and total sales of 78.19 billion rupiah, she said.
The company also achieved sales of 12,197 tonnes of rubber at an average selling price of $1,502 per tonne for total sales of 42.79 billion rupiah.

Lonsum had also locked in prices for more than 70 percent of its 1996 final quarter crude palm oil sales at $540 per tonne and 98 percent of rubber sales at a minimum of $1,332 per tonne, Safford said.
The company had also locked in prices of $520 per tonne for 31.8 percent of its 1997 CPO production and $1,382 per tonne for its 1997 rubber production.

London Sumatra is among Indonesia's largest plantation firms. It operates 19 plantations totalling nearly 55,000 hectares in North Sumatra, Java and Sulawesi. It cultivates, harvests, and processes palm oil, rubber, cocoa, tea and coffee.
